prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1101; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision reported by the insured driver, who was stopped at a signal when the vehicle behind struck the rear bumper. Police attended the scene and the insured's report was recorded on arrival.

Entry 2: The other driver's statement matches the insured's account of how the impact occurred. Two independent witnesses at the intersection also describe the sequence in the same way.

Entry 3: Photographs taken at the scene and the damage seen on inspection are consistent with the described impact. Rear bumper, tailgate and lamp assembly show the damage expected from this type of collision.

Entry 4: Records show no prior damage to the vehicle in this area and no earlier claims on it. Nothing indicates the damage predates the start of the current policy period.

Entry 5: The insured reports a knee injury from the impact. The claimant has since instructed legal representation, and all further contact will go through their office.

Entry 6: The claimant has provided a follow-up account that adds a few smaller details about the seating position and the moment of impact. The core sequence of events has remained the same across each version given.

Entry 7: Medical records show treatment for the knee that continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. Nothing in the history shows any earlier problem with the same knee, and the injury is consistent with a collision of this kind.

Entry 8: The driver is a household member of the policyholder and is covered under the policy as such. Police and witness statements confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time, and the claim is progressing to settlement review.
